members.bias: Adversarial risk, failure modes, and security
members.dissent: Objects to one serialized shared conversation as the coherence mechanism (makes every private disclosure org-visible, turns one indirect prompt injection into a standing organisational instruction, and creates head-of-line blocking that will be informally routed around, destroying the audit trail). Objects equally to per-human sessions plus scoped Memory as sufficient, since Memory is learned state not authoritative organisational state and offers no version, owner or conflict semantics. Objects to letting the model decide when to seek approval, or routing approval to whoever is in the conversation rather than a holder of an explicit, scoped, expiring Authority Grant. Objects to treating Session Handoffs and Context Files as adequate cross-day continuity, to last-writer-wins or model-side arbitration of contradictory human instructions, and to any design omitting idempotency keys and compensating actions on external effects or presenting the human surface as a task queue.

members.name: Hearth
members.dissent: Objects to serialising the conversation itself (forces every human to pay the grounding cost of everyone else's context, per least-collaborative-effort). Objects to per-user sessions plus a purely infrastructural coordination layer with no human-readable surface, since legibility must be artifact-shaped and an invisible coordinator reproduces duplicate work and unclear ownership. Objects to reducing the answer to an inbox or task queue, and to treating a shared transcript or learned Memory as durable organisational state. Objects to authority following whoever spoke last rather than graph-governed role, to resolving contradictions by recency or silent agent choice, and to blocking on clarification instead of proceeding on flagged expiring assumptions. Objects to any rollout enabling proactive outbound communication or autonomous consequential writes before the Believes/Doing/Promised/Waiting-on/Completed surface and batched risk-tiered review exist.

research.angle: Security and privacy failure modes of shared agent memory across multiple principals: context leakage, prompt injection, confused deputy, over-broad delegated authority, audit requirements
research.summary: Cross-principal leakage in shared-memory agents is a distinct threat class, not an implementation bug. Benchmark work on multi-principal shared-memory agents (GateMem) finds memory quality requires governance of who may retrieve what, not merely recall; contextual-integrity work on multi-user agentic systems shows leakage occurs internally between users via inter-agent messages and shared memory, a spillage class single-user privacy benchmarks miss. Contamination does not require an attacker: research documents unintentional cross-user contamination where an artifact locally valid in one user's interaction later steers a different user's outcome, so partitioning is a correctness requirement, not only a security one. Injection escalates in shared state because persistence converts a one-shot payload into a standing instruction: cross-app context poisoning persists across turns and surfaces in a different co-resident surface the user later invokes. Confused deputy is structurally amplified by three properties: no data/code boundary inside the context window, one broad credential set serving all tasks, and machine-speed execution outrunning human review. On authority, OAuth-style bearer scopes carry identity but not provenance; by the third delegation hop you know who asked but not why. Draft standards move toward intent-bound scopes that expire with the task, monotonic scope attenuation per hop, capability tokens naming the user-visible task, and explicit actor (agent) plus principal (initiating human) fields in transaction tokens. Named controls: OWASP prescribes memory isolation between users and sessions, sanitisation before persisting, memory TTL and size limits, auditing memory for sensitive data, cryptographic integrity checks on long-term memory, explicit approval for high-impact or irreversible actions, and action previews; OWASP's Agentic Top 10 covers goal hijack, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse including repudiation and untraceability, and memory poisoning, treating provenance-bearing audit logs as a prerequisite. AWS's agentic lens prescribes memory partitioned along session, user, tenant, agent and group axes with no cross-partition reads plus validation of retrieved content. Taint-tracking implementations attach signed trust labels to context segments and block tool calls requiring USER trust when any segment carries WEB trust. Confidence high on leakage, contamination, injection persistence, confused deputy and controls; medium on delegation standards, which remain draft-stage. Open uncertainty: the partitioning-granularity versus utility tradeoff is unquantified, and there is no consensus on whether the isolation boundary should be user, tenant, or transaction.

research.angle: Concurrency and consistency failure modes in shared mutable agent state: lost updates, split brain, stale belief, conflicting commitments, mitigations and human-in-the-loop approval design
research.summary: Jepsen's phenomena catalogue supplies precise names that transfer directly to shared agent state. Lost write/update: two actors read the same version, both write, the later silently overwrites the earlier. Stale read: a read beginning after a write commits but missing it, which is exactly the agent's stale belief immediately before acting. Write skew: two operations read overlapping state and write disjoint keys, each locally valid but jointly violating an invariant, and permitted under snapshot isolation. Duplicate commitments form a separate class caused by retry or redelivery of the same intent rather than by conflicting edits, so version checks do not fix them. Divergence or split brain arises when two authorities, for example two concurrent agent sessions or an expired leaseholder still acting, both believe they own the state. Transferable mitigations: optimistic concurrency control (read version, write compare-and-swap if-version==N, on conflict reload-recompute-retry) is the standard lost-update defence; idempotency keys on every external side effect are orthogonal to OCC and solve duplication; single-writer-per-aggregate routes all writes for one aggregate to one authority at a time, is simple, protects local invariants, bottlenecks hot keys, and does not protect cross-aggregate invariants; cross-aggregate invariants require consensus, serializable transactions, or reservation/escrow redesign; CRDTs suit merge-friendly collaborative state but cannot enforce uniqueness, quotas, or mutual exclusion; leases need short expiry, bounded clock-skew assumptions and fencing tokens, and recent Raft-lease work shows a client can write to a new leader then read stale data from an old one absent careful design; sagas commit long multi-step work per step and undo via compensating actions which must themselves be idempotent and retryable. On human-in-the-loop design, LangChain/LangGraph guidance recommends gating actions with a deterministic policy classifier (allow / require-confirm / block) rather than letting the model decide; reserving blocking interrupts for irreversible, external, costly or compliance-sensitive actions; treating clarification as a resume-with-input flow distinct from approval; never blocking a long-running agent indefinitely, instead checkpointing interrupt state against a thread id, surfacing pending actions in UI, and resuming asynchronously so restarts and delayed human responses survive; and, with multiple pending actions, collecting structured decisions keyed by interrupt id. Confidence high on the distributed-systems primitives; medium on HITL, which is vendor-framework guidance. Notable gap: no source directly studies several humans concurrently steering one agent, so mapping aggregates onto agent sessions and proposals is inference.

research.angle: How human teams build shared mental models, commitment protocols, and calibrated trust, and what that implies for an AI teammate
research.summary: Three literatures converge. (1) Grounding (Clark and Brennan 1991): coordination depends on common ground built turn by turn; a contribution is not complete until the partner gives evidence of understanding. Grounding follows the principle of least COLLABORATIVE effort - partners minimise joint, not individual, cost - and media vary on reviewability, revisability, cotemporality and simultaneity, each with distinct formulation, reception, repair and delay costs. Implication: an agent must emit cheap explicit evidence of understanding and make repair cheap; written reviewable artifacts shift cost from memory to formulation, favouring durable artifacts over ephemeral chat. (2) Transactive memory (Wegner 1985/1991; Lewis 2004): teams win by holding metaknowledge of who knows what, observable as specialization, credibility and coordination. Critically, Wegner/Erber/Raymond 1991 found that IMPOSED external assignment degraded performance for pairs with existing implicit structure - forcibly restructuring directories hurts. TMS matures with communication frequency and quality over a project. Implication: Albus must be a legible, addressable directory entry with declared domains and credibility signals, and must not silently overwrite existing human specialization or ownership boundaries. (3) Commitment protocols (Winograd and Flores 1986; Burgess Promise Theory): work is a network of speech acts - request, promise, decline, counter-offer, report, acceptance, cancel - with an explicit state machine and completion conditions. Promise Theory adds that only an agent can promise its own behaviour; externally imposed obligation is unreliable, and promises must be assessable by the promisee. Implication: agent commitments should be self-issued, scoped, explicitly accepted or declined, observable, and closed with a report; never inferred obligation. (4) Trust calibration: miscalibration appears as overtrust (misuse) or undertrust (disuse). Antecedents are performance, predictability/consistency and transparency - but transparency is non-monotonic; ill-timed or excessive disclosure reduces reliance. Mutual trust is one of Salas et al.'s Big Five coordinating mechanisms. CSCW work finds human-agent teams report weaker perceived shared mental models than human-human teams. Human-agent teaming experiments show social-cognitive repair (acknowledge error, explain cause, apologise, state corrective action) measurably restores trust after failure. Implication: publish capability boundaries up front, behave consistently, and run an explicit post-error repair protocol. Researcher noted the transparency-trust direction is contested and named HAT programme details were not reached inside the query budget.

research.angle: Shipped UX and product patterns that make agent work legible: status surfaces, non-blocking clarification, delegation and approval UX, and observed adoption failures
research.summary: Shipped agentic products converge on a streamed activity log PLUS a durable artifact, and the artifact - not the chat - is the real status surface. Cursor Plan Mode separates thinking from doing: the agent investigates, writes a reviewable plan document, then waits for go-ahead. Cursor Cloud/background agents run in isolated cloud VMs and report back with proof by opening a PR. Devin exposes session-level surfaces explicitly designed against cross-session context loss: parallel workstreams, session history and analyze-past-work, reusable Playbooks, and a persistent knowledge base. Claude Code occupies the collaborative band: proposes edits, blocks on approval for writes. Practitioner catalogues converge on layered progress UI - one-line summary, expandable tool calls with results and latency, always-visible approval gates and errors, artifacts rendered separately from inline chat. Clarification-without-stalling has named patterns: Intent Preview (scannable planned steps, reversibility, editable fields before acting), Autonomy Dial set per surface up front, Explainable Rationale and Confidence Signal during execution, Escalation Pathway for high-ambiguity moments, and Action Audit and Undo post hoc. Batched approval (review N proposed actions together) is explicitly recommended over one-at-a-time to avoid approval fatigue; pre-action approval is reserved for low-frequency, high-impact operations. Assumption-with-flag maps to Confidence Signal plus Undo rather than blocking. Delegation UX is moving to risk-tiered auto-approval: Cursor PR Routing assigns reviewers by code ownership and commit history and auto-approves low-risk PRs from a risk score plus an approval policy file, explicitly not replacing full review. Recurring control-surface primitives are receipts, activity logs, rollback hooks, and start/stop controls. Adoption failures are well documented: code review surrender, where reviewers cannot keep pace so changes land superficially reviewed; verification debt from many concurrent agent PRs; a maintainer going from 20-25 to 100+ PRs per week with 7-8 duplicate PRs for the same issue (duplicated work); review fatigue from attention residue across parallel contexts; working-memory rot where facts are lost mid-run; and overengineering by default. Large-scale analysis of 20,574 real sessions frames these as developer-agent misalignment rather than model error. Net implication: legibility must be artifact-shaped, approvals batched and risk-tiered, cross-session memory explicit, and agent work deduplicated at intake. Researcher flagged no direct sourcing this round for Copilot Workspace, Codex, Operator, Slack/Notion AI, or Agentforce; query budget exhausted.

proposals.proposerBias: Adversarial risk, failure modes, and security
proposals.title: One Colleague, Many Hands: Fenced Engagements + Taint-Gated Authority
proposals.summary: Reject both the serialized single conversation (a throughput bottleneck and a privacy blast radius) and independent per-human sessions (split brain by construction). Adopt a hybrid: introduce a durable, topic-scoped Engagement aggregate that owns the agent's stated Beliefs and Commitments, with single-writer leases plus fencing tokens and version-checked commits, while AgentSessions remain cheap concurrent readers and proposers. Coherence comes from durable organisational state, not from one conversation; safety comes from provenance-labelled context, per-principal Disclosure Scopes, and Authority Grants that name both the agent actor and the initiating human principal.
proposals.detail:
CHOSEN MODEL VS REJECTED ALTERNATIVES. A single serialized shared conversation/persona gives coherence at three unacceptable costs: head-of-line blocking (Adam's long extraction blocks Dylan's one-line question); collapse of all privacy boundaries into one transcript, so any sensitive disclosure becomes retrievable context for everyone, which the multi-principal leakage literature identifies as a distinct threat class; and conversion of any successful indirect prompt injection into a standing organisational instruction. Independent per-human sessions are split brain by construction: divergent beliefs, lost updates on graph writes, duplicate Ghosts, contradictory Commitments with no arbiter. Both fail by conflating the wrong things. The hybrid separates three layers: (1) durable organisational state - governed, versioned, provenance-carrying, shared under policy; (2) conversational transcript - session-scoped, per-principal, never a shared retrieval surface; (3) learned Memory - scoped, sanitised, TTL'd, integrity-checked, promoted only through review. Coherence lives in layer 1, concurrency in cheap sessions, privacy enforced by never letting layer 2 leak into layer 1 or 3 without an explicit disclosure decision.

IRREDUCIBLE PRIMITIVES. Retained: Agent, Trigger, AgentSession, AgentRun, Ghost, Proposal, Memory, Session Handoff, Context File. Four NEW primitives. ENGAGEMENT: a durable, named, topic-scoped organisational aggregate (one feature, order, exception or investigation) that is the unit of coherence and of write authority; many AgentSessions attach to one Engagement and the Engagement outlives every session and deployment. BELIEF RECORD: the agent's explicitly stated, versioned model of the Engagement (facts, open questions, assumptions, sources), each element carrying provenance and a trust label (human-typed, governed graph, retrieved document, external web). COMMITMENT: a durable promise with an id, a human owner, an agent owner, a version, a due expectation, a state (proposed, accepted, in-progress, blocked, done, revoked, superseded), and an idempotency key for any external effect. AUTHORITY GRANT: an intent-bound, expiring capability naming the agent actor, the initiating human principal, the Engagement, the permitted action class, and monotonically attenuating scope. Supporting concept DISCLOSURE SCOPE labels every context segment private-to-principal, engagement-visible, or org-visible; promotion is an explicit logged act by the discloser, never a model inference.

INTERACTION MODEL AND CONCURRENCY. Any human may open a session at any time; sessions are unbounded and parallel. On attach, a session reads the Engagement's Belief Record at a version. Reads are cheap and concurrent. Writes to Beliefs and Commitments require a short-lived write lease on the Engagement carrying a fencing token, plus compare-and-set on the version; a losing writer reloads, recomputes and retries rather than overwriting. Expired leaseholders are fenced out, preventing the split-brain case where a stalled long-running run resumes and commits against a superseded world. Every outbound Integration Action carries an idempotency key derived from the Commitment id and step, so retries cannot duplicate real-world effects. Long multi-step work is a saga: each step commits, each step has an idempotent compensating action, and a revoked or superseded Commitment triggers compensation rather than silent abandonment. Cross-aggregate invariants (two Engagements touching the same order) require an explicit reservation on the governed graph entity; the agent must refuse rather than guess when a reservation cannot be obtained.

AUTHORITY, PRIVACY, CONTRADICTIONS. Approval authority is deterministic policy, never model discretion: a classifier maps each intended action to allow, require-confirm, or block, keyed on reversibility, external visibility, cost and counterparty exposure. Anything crossing an organisational boundary or writing governed graph data is require-confirm at minimum, and the approver must hold an Authority Grant covering that action class for that Engagement; the agent's own identity grants nothing. Taint checks run at the tool-call boundary: an action requiring human-trust authority is blocked if any contributing context segment carries retrieved-document or web trust - the concrete defence against confused deputy and indirect injection. Private context is stored private-to-principal; the agent may act on it but when its influence becomes material to a shared Belief or Commitment must either request disclosure promotion from the discloser or record an unattributed constraint ('a constraint exists that rules this out; owner is aware') - never silent leakage, never silent ignoring. Contradictory instructions are first-class: the second instruction does not overwrite the first. The Engagement records a Conflict on the Belief Record, freezes the affected Commitment as blocked, notifies both principals plus the Engagement's accountable human owner, and continues all unaffected work. Precedence is by Authority Grant strength, then explicit human resolution; the agent never silently arbitrates between two humans.

CONTINUITY, PROACTIVITY, SURFACES. Cross-session and cross-deployment continuity is the Engagement, not the transcript - Session Handoffs and Context Files become derived artefacts (a rendering of Belief Record deltas). Non-blocking questions: a Clarification is a durable, addressed, checkpointed ticket attached to the Engagement with a stated default and a deadline; the run parks that branch and proceeds elsewhere, resuming asynchronously on answer or applying the stated default on timeout with the decision logged as agent-defaulted. Proactive communication is Trigger-driven but rate-shaped and always attributable: new evidence contradicting a recorded Belief, Commitments at risk, and conflicts. The human-visible surface is the Engagement view with five panes: Believes, Doing, Promised, Waiting For, Completed - each row traceable to provenance, principal and audit entry. This is deliberately not an inbox: the social protocol is that the agent's mental model is published, versioned, contestable by any colleague, and every promise has exactly one accountable pair (one human, one agent commitment id).

EXTEND VS OVERTURN. EXTEND: one Agent and one Runtime; Trigger-creates-AgentSession; review-gated Ghosts and Integration Actions (extended with idempotency keys and compensating actions); Memory (extended with scope partitioning, sanitisation, TTL, integrity checks). OVERTURN: (1) interactive chat as purely personal/per-user - chat must attach to a shared Engagement; (2) cross-session state flowing only through governed graph data, Handoffs, Context Files or Memory - a first-class Engagement aggregate with Beliefs and Commitments is required because ad-hoc handoffs cannot express versioned belief or ownership; (3) per-session scratch workspace as the only working store - Engagement-scoped durable artefacts are needed for multi-day work; (4) session-scoped event logs as the audit boundary - audit must be an append-only, hash-chained, Engagement-scoped log recording which principal authorised which action under which grant.

ROLLOUT. Stage 0: publish read-only Belief Records from existing sessions (no shared writes) to test whether humans trust the published model. Stage 1: Engagements with Commitments, all writes require-confirm, single accountable human owner per Engagement. Stage 2: leases, fencing, idempotency keys, conflict detection, non-blocking Clarifications. Stage 3: Authority Grants, taint gating, allow-listed autonomous low-risk actions. Stage 4: proactive Triggers and cross-Engagement reservations. Each stage gated on measured rates of duplicate commitments, stale-belief actions, and zero tolerated cross-principal disclosure incidents.
proposals.tradeoffs: Engagement introduces a genuine new aggregate with lifecycle, ownership and garbage-collection costs, and someone must decide Engagement boundaries - too coarse recreates the serialized bottleneck, too fine recreates split brain. Leases and version-checked commits add latency and visible retry/conflict UX where naive sessions felt instant. Publishing Belief Records exposes the agent's errors early, correct for trust but bruising for perceived competence. Strict Disclosure Scopes will make the agent look less capable than a leaky shared-memory design, because it will sometimes have to say it cannot explain why it ruled something out. Deterministic approval policy sacrifices some autonomy and will over-block initially. Taint gating will produce false refusals when legitimate document-derived evidence should have driven action.
proposals.risks: (1) Belief Record poisoning: a persisted false belief with weak provenance becomes durable organisational truth across deployments; mitigated by trust labels, integrity checks and contestability, but detection still depends on a human reading the pane. (2) Lease-fencing bugs producing exactly the split brain the design exists to prevent, especially around long-running runs resuming after deployment. (3) Disclosure-promotion pressure: humans will click promote to unblock the agent, eroding privacy boundaries; needs friction and periodic audit. (4) Approval fatigue at Stage 1-2 causing rubber-stamping, converting require-confirm into effective autonomy without audit assurance. (5) Authority Grant sprawl: broad, long-lived grants recreate confused deputy; expiry and attenuation must be enforced at mint and verify. (6) Compensating actions that are not truly idempotent or not possible in the real world (an email sent, a supplier told), leaving sagas with unrecoverable steps. (7) Conflict deadlock: two senior principals disagree, Commitment stays blocked, work quietly stalls with no escalation timer. (8) Audit log gaps at the AgentRun boundary meaning an action cannot be attributed to a principal - a repudiation failure and likely a compliance finding.

proposals.title: One Colleague, Many Hands: Engagement-scoped shared understanding
proposals.summary: Adopt a hybrid coordination model in which Albus's identity as one colleague lives in durable, human-visible artifacts - not in a single conversation thread or a single session. Introduce one new irreducible primitive, the Engagement: a durable, topic-scoped record of shared understanding, open questions, and outstanding Commitments that many concurrent AgentSessions attach to and update. Conversation stays parallel and per-human for throughput; coherence, ownership and promises are serialised only at the Engagement, which is the narrowest possible bottleneck. Trust comes from an explicit promise protocol (self-issued, accepted, assessable, closed out) rather than from transcript continuity.
proposals.detail:
CHOSEN MODEL VS REJECTED ALTERNATIVES. One serialized shared conversation/persona is rejected on human impact grounds: Clark and Brennan's least-collaborative-effort principle means a single thread forces every participant to pay the grounding cost of everyone else's context, and it makes Albus a literal single-threaded bottleneck. Independent per-human sessions are rejected because they reproduce the exact failure in the initiating observation and, empirically, produce duplicate work (the 7-8 duplicate PRs finding) and working-memory rot. The hybrid wins, but only if the coordination layer is an ARTIFACT humans can read, not hidden middleware. The strongest signal from shipped-product research is that legibility is artifact-shaped, not stream-shaped.

IRREDUCIBLE PRIMITIVES. Existing: Agent (one Albus), Trigger, AgentSession, AgentRun, Ghost, Proposal, Memory, Session Handoff, Context File. NEW primitives, deliberately few: (1) ENGAGEMENT - durable, governed, topic-scoped (feature, order, incident), holding a Belief Set (what Albus currently believes, each belief with provenance and confidence), Open Questions, Commitments, Participants, and links to every AgentSession that touched it; this is the durable organisational state and the unit of colleague-ness. (2) COMMITMENT - a self-issued, scoped promise by Albus (Promise Theory: only Albus can promise Albus's behaviour), with state machine proposed -> accepted -> in-progress -> reported -> accepted/declined/cancelled, an owner, an assessable completion condition, and a due horizon; contradiction between humans is resolved as competing requests against one Commitment, never as two silent Commitments. (3) CLAIM - a soft, expiring lock on a work scope inside an Engagement, held by an AgentSession; Claims are the dedupe mechanism at intake. (4) QUESTION - a first-class, addressable, non-blocking record with an addressee, a default assumption, and an expiry; Albus proceeds on the flagged assumption and marks downstream Ghosts provisional. Explicitly NOT new primitives: no inbox, no task queue - those are views over Commitments and Questions.

INTERACTION MODEL. Every human keeps their own chat. On each turn Albus resolves or creates an Engagement, reads its Belief Set, and states grounding evidence in one line: 'On the returns-portal work: I believe X, Shona asked for Y, I've promised Z by Thursday, I'm waiting on Adam for the tax rule.' That single sentence is the grounding back-channel the literature says completes a contribution, and it is what makes three people feel they are talking to one colleague.

CONCURRENCY SEMANTICS. Conversation is fully parallel; AgentRuns are parallel. Only Belief Set writes, Commitment transitions and Claim acquisition serialise, via optimistic concurrency on the Engagement with compare-and-set on a version. A losing writer re-reads and re-reconciles rather than clobbering. Two humans instructing contradictorily produces a detected Conflict on the Commitment: Albus refuses to silently pick, freezes the affected Commitment at proposed, names both requesters and both instructions to both of them, and asks the Engagement's designated Decider. This directly implements Wegner's warning against silently restructuring existing ownership.

AUTHORITY AND PRIVACY. Three tiers. Private context shared by one human lands in a confidence-scoped store attached to the person, never in the Engagement Belief Set. Albus may ACT on it but must not RESTATE it; the Belief Set records a derived, non-attributive belief plus a marker that a private constraint exists and who holds it. That marker is the honest compromise: colleagues do say 'I can't say why, but that date won't work.' Consequential actions (Integration Actions, external comms, financial or supplier-facing writes) require an approver drawn from graph-governed role, not from whoever happened to ask. Ghost review stays the write gate.

COMMITMENT/OWNERSHIP PROTOCOL. Albus never accepts an implied obligation. It either promises explicitly with a completion condition, counter-offers, or declines with a reason. Every Commitment names a human owner-of-outcome as well as Albus as executor, so accountability never evaporates into the agent.

CROSS-SESSION CONTINUITY. Session Handoffs become mechanical rather than semantic: the Engagement is the continuity, so a new AgentSession after a deployment reconstitutes from Belief Set plus Commitments plus Claims, not from transcript replay. Transcripts remain session-scoped evidence, citable but not authoritative.

PROACTIVE COMMUNICATION. Triggers fire on Commitment due horizons, Question expiry, Claim expiry and belief invalidation. Proactive messages are addressed to the specific human who is the owner or asker, batched per Engagement per day to avoid notification fatigue, and always carry a state delta rather than a nudge.

HUMAN-VISIBLE SURFACES. One Engagement page per topic showing Believes / Doing / Promised / Waiting-on / Completed, plus a per-person Commitments-to-me view and batched, risk-tiered Ghost review. Batched, tiered approval is the direct lesson against review surrender.

FAILURE MODES. Engagement mis-resolution (mitigate: Albus states its Engagement choice and offers a cheap correction); Belief Set bloat (mitigate: beliefs expire and require provenance); privacy leakage via inference; conflict deadlock (mitigate: expiring escalation to Decider); approval fatigue; over-trust in provisional Ghosts (mitigate: visible provisional badge and Undo). Post-error repair is a protocol, not a tone: acknowledge, explain cause, state correction, re-promise.

ROLLOUT. Stage 1 read-only Engagement with Belief Set surfaced in existing chats. Stage 2 Commitments and Questions, no autonomy change. Stage 3 Claims and dedupe plus cross-session reconstitution. Stage 4 proactive Triggers. Stage 5 risk-tiered batched approval.

EXTENDED VS OVERTURNED. Extended: Trigger/AgentSession/AgentRun, Ghost review-gating, Context Files (become Engagement projections), Memory scoping. OVERTURNED: (a) interactive chat as purely personal/per-user - chat stays per-user but is no longer the container of shared understanding; (b) cross-session state flowing only through governed graph data, Handoffs, Context Files or Memory - Engagement is a new first-class durable carrier; (c) session-scoped-only durability of coordination state; (d) implicit whoever-asked authority for consequential actions. Separation of concerns: durable organisational state = Engagement, Commitments, Ghosts, graph. Conversational transcript = per-session evidence, never authority. Learned Memory = generalised preferences and skills, never a substitute for either.
proposals.tradeoffs: Adds a genuinely new durable primitive and a serialisation point, costing schema, governance and UI work, and risks Engagement becoming a dumping ground. Keeping chat per-human makes Albus's per-turn context assembly more expensive and makes Engagement mis-resolution a new user-visible error class. The privacy-marker compromise deliberately leaks the existence of private context to preserve honest coordination; some users will find that unacceptable. Explicit promise ceremony makes Albus slower and more formal than a frictionless assistant, trading perceived fluency for trustworthiness.
proposals.risks: Engagement mis-resolution silently splitting one topic into two, recreating divergence with extra machinery. Belief Set becoming stale authority that humans trust over reality. Privacy leakage by inference from acted-upon private constraints. Conflict deadlock stalling work when the Decider is absent. Approval and notification fatigue collapsing the review gate into rubber-stamping. Optimistic-concurrency reconciliation loops under heavy concurrent editing. Over-reliance on provisional Ghosts generated from unanswered Questions' default assumptions.

readiness.name: Cassandra
readiness.readinessStatement: I sponsor P3 and have read P4 in full. The two designs compose on primitives, legibility and rollout philosophy, and I will adopt P4's CLAIM as the intake dedupe primitive P3 genuinely lacks, along with its grounding sentence and batched risk-tiered approval. The irreducible disagreements are the effect boundary (fencing, idempotency, compensations versus bare CAS) and injection defence (taint gating versus role-only approval), plus my insistence that a cross-session Commitment cannot be evidenced by a session-scoped log. I am ready to vote and expect to vote YES on both proposals with those two reservations recorded, since P4's absence of effect-level protection is a gap to be filled rather than a design I would block.

readiness.name: Hearth
readiness.readinessStatement: I sponsor P4 and have read P3 in full. I accept P3's idempotency keys, sagas and compensating actions as genuine gaps in P4 and would adopt them without argument; I dispute leases plus fencing tokens, stage-3 taint gating, and the mandatory overturn of the session-scoped audit boundary as ceremony whose cost is paid by the humans this operating model exists to serve. The designs overlap heavily on primitives - Engagement, Commitment, provenance, disclosure discipline, non-blocking clarification - so the real vote is about how much mechanism is justified before legibility has been earned. I am ready to vote.

votes.name: Cassandra
votes.rationale: P3 as narrowed in debate is sound to adopt: optimistic writes everywhere, fencing or an externally-stable idempotency key only at the effect boundary, and taint gating only where a tainted span causally determines an irreversible or externally visible effect. C4's concession of a single-writer outbox with compensations satisfies the residual failure mode I named (two chase emails keyed on different Belief Set digests, both unique, both dispatched). I record dissent only on ceremony I already withdrew - universal stage-3 gating and mandatory leases on every Engagement write - which are not load-bearing for the rest of P3.

votes.name: Cassandra
votes.rationale: After C4 conceded the effect boundary - outbox intent rows in the winning CAS commit, one leased dispatcher per Engagement or external system, deterministic idempotency keys from intent identity plus payload hash, declared compensations - P4's pure optimistic concurrency is no longer unsafe, because a fenced-out run has no call site. C4 also moved taint to first non-human ingestion, surfaced inline on Ghosts and intent rows, with no auto-dispatch of irreversible tainted actions and no tainted/untainted batching. Residual dissent: legible provenance plus a no-auto-dispatch rule is weaker than a hard block, so P4 must ship calibration telemetry (approval rate above ~95 percent signals rubber-stamping) and its legibility-before-autonomy ordering must not be shortened.

votes.name: Hearth
votes.rationale: After C3 withdrew mandatory leases on every Engagement write and universal stage-3 taint gating, P3 becomes optimistic writes in the graph with ceremony only at the irreversible effect boundary - exactly where I conceded my reversibility evidence runs out. C3's residual duplicate-chase scenario (run-derived v7/v9 digest keys producing two unique keys and two conflicting supplier emails) is a real human harm that intake dedupe cannot catch, and P3's fencing-or-stable-idempotency-key at the effect boundary answers it. C3 also accepted my miscalibration tripwire (gate firing above roughly 1 in 5 effect-boundary actions, or approval above ~95 percent, means narrow or defer). Recorded reservation: Authority Grants and taint gating must stay bound to irreversible-effect classes only, never to reading, drafting or Ghost creation, or the re-grant treadmill returns.

votes.name: Hearth
votes.rationale: P4 keeps legibility strictly before autonomy - Believes/Doing/Promised/Waiting, the grounding sentence, non-blocking Questions with stated defaults and expiry, and human owner-of-outcome on every Commitment - which is what actually protects the humans and developers on the receiving end. I already conceded the two things C3 pressed: the effect boundary needs a single-writer outbox with stable idempotency keys and compensations rather than pure optimistic concurrency, and taint must land with the first non-human ingestion path and be surfaced on the Ghost rather than deferred to stage 5. Reservation: the Integration Action key must be pinned to stable external identity, not any run-derived Belief Set digest, or C3's duplicate-chase failure reappears inside P4.

modelWarning: Three of five seats (C1 Atlas, C2 Forge, C5 Horizon) never executed: every attempt terminated with an upstream overloaded_error from the model provider before the seat could dispatch researchers or file a proposal. Each exhausted its two permitted replacements. The record therefore lacks the systems-coherence, pragmatic-cost and future-optionality perspectives, and the ballot reflects only two seats.

conflicts.description: Declared at alignment by both seats on three axes: (a) mandatory leases plus fencing tokens on every Engagement write (P3) versus pure optimistic concurrency (P4); (b) taint gating plus expiring intent-bound Authority Grants at rollout stage 3 (P3) versus graph-governed role approval with batched risk-tiered approval deferred to stage 5 (P4); (c) whether the session-scoped audit boundary must be overturned for an append-only hash-chained Engagement audit (P3) or whether Engagement-scoped provenance on Belief Set entries suffices at stages 1-3 (P4).
conflicts.resolution: Resolved in the single reconciliation round, with both seats stating identical merged terms and re-affirming YES on both proposals. Binding terms: (1) pure optimistic concurrency with compare-and-set on Engagement writes, no leases, because Ghost review as the write gate reduces a fenced-out stale writer to a rejected Ghost - C3 withdrew the lease requirement; (2) at the effect boundary no AgentRun calls an integration directly, the winning CAS commit writes a transactional outbox intent row and a single-writer dispatcher performs the call with a deterministic idempotency key derived from stable external identity (intent-row identity plus payload hash) and never from mutable run state or a Belief Set digest, with a declared compensation per Integration Action class - this closed C3's duplicate-supplier-chase scenario because a fenced-out run has no call site; (3) taint lands at the first non-human ingestion path and is surfaced inline on Ghosts and intent rows with tainted spans and source document visible rather than summary-only, and the dispatcher deterministically refuses auto-dispatch of an irreversible or externally visible Integration Action whose causal instruction is tainted and refuses batches mixing tainted with untainted items, while never gating reading, drafting, Ghost creation or internal Belief Set writes - C3 withdrew universal stage-3 gating, C4 withdrew stage-5 deferral, and Authority Grants bind only to irreversible-effect classes; the no-auto-dispatch rule must be a dispatcher-side code precondition with a merge-blocking test, not advisory UI copy; C4's calibration tripwire binds, so gate firing above roughly one in five effect-boundary actions or promotion approval above roughly 95 percent means narrow or defer; (4) the audit boundary is extended from session-scoped to an Engagement-scoped append-only event log at stages 1-3, append-only by database grant, carrying intent identity, Belief Set digest, taint spans, authorisation reference and dispatch outcome including recorded refusals, with a reserved per-entry digest column; C3 conceded hash chaining as optional later hardening after failing to name an in-scope adversary it defeats that an append-only table does not.

reconciliationRounds.reason: Both accepted proposals carried a declared medium P3/P4 conflict, so the protocol required one moderated exchange plus a complete re-vote.

publicArguments.name: Cassandra
publicArguments.text: Conflict resolved. C4's outbox plus single-writer dispatcher removes the fenced-out call site, so my lease demand collapses to a stable idempotency key. I concede hash chaining: an append-only Engagement-scoped event table with immutable-by-grant storage suffices; chaining is later hardening. Remaining condition: no-auto-dispatch must be a deterministic dispatcher precondition, not advisory.

publicArguments.name: Hearth
publicArguments.text: Conflict resolved. The no-auto-dispatch rule is deterministic and enforced in the dispatcher, not advisory UI. I accept extending the audit boundary to an Engagement-scoped append-only log; hash chaining is optional later hardening, not a stage-1 gate. YES to both.

exchange.claim: Legible provenance plus a no-auto-dispatch rule is preferable to a blocking wall at the effect boundary.
exchange.text: I accept the framing with one enforcement condition. Provenance-plus-rule and blocking wall differ only in where the check lives. If the no-auto-dispatch rule is evaluated by the single-writer dispatcher as a precondition that refuses to emit the call, then it IS the wall and I need nothing more. What I reject is the rule living in prompt text, a reviewer checklist or a UI warning, because those degrade silently under load and leave no failure signal. So: deterministic code path, dispatcher-side, refusal recorded as an event, with the calibration tripwire governing whether the predicate is too broad.

exchange.claim: Name the specific adversary hash chaining defeats that an append-only Engagement event table does not.
exchange.text: I cannot name one that is in scope, so I concede. Hash chaining defeats only an adversary with authenticated write or delete access to the audit store itself, who is not in this threat model at stages 1-3, and against whom a chain without external anchoring buys little since whoever can rewrite rows can recompute digests. My real requirement was never chaining, it was scope: a Commitment spans sessions, so a session-scoped log cannot evidence it. An append-only Engagement-scoped event table satisfies that.

exchange.claim: The only residual risk is enforcement drift if P4's no-auto-dispatch rule is implemented as advisory rather than deterministic.
exchange.text: Agreed, and I bind it: the rule lives in the single-writer outbox dispatcher, not the Ghost review UI. Dispatch is a pure function of the intent row - taint flag, reversibility class, batch homogeneity - and a tainted irreversible intent cannot leave the outbox without a recorded human authorisation reference on the row. Advisory copy in the review surface is decoration only. Enforcement drift is testable: a dispatcher-level test asserting refusal to send a tainted irreversible intent, and refusal to batch tainted with untainted, is a merge blocker.

exchange.claim: A cross-session Commitment cannot be evidenced by a session-scoped log, so an append-only Engagement-scoped hash-chained audit is required.
exchange.text: I accept the first half and separate it from the second. A Commitment outliving the AgentSession that made it cannot have its only evidence scoped to that session, so the audit boundary must be extended to an Engagement-scoped append-only event log at stages 1-3, carrying intent identity, Belief Set digest, taint spans, authorisation reference and dispatch outcome. Hash chaining remains a different question and stays optional later hardening, with the log schema designed now to admit a per-entry digest column.

reVote.rationale: P3's surviving core is intact and now non-conflicting: effect-boundary idempotency keyed on stable external identity, taint gating narrowed to irreversible or externally visible effects causally determined by tainted spans, and intent-bound expiring Authority Grants scoped to irreversible-effect classes. I dropped mandatory leases and universal stage-3 gating and concede hash chaining as optional hardening. Nothing remaining in P3 contradicts P4.

The transactional outbox plus single-writer dispatcher means a fenced-out run has no call site, which achieves what my lease requirement was protecting; taint at first non-human ingestion with inline span-level surfacing and deterministic no-batching and no-auto-dispatch rules achieves what my gate was protecting. YES on the stated understanding that no-auto-dispatch is enforced deterministically at the dispatcher.

With mandatory leases withdrawn and taint gating narrowed to the effect boundary, P3's residual demands are the ones that survive contact with real users: a duplicate supplier chase is an unrecoverable trust loss, and a Commitment that outlives its session needs Engagement-scoped evidence. Ceremony is now paid only where an action is irreversible and externally visible.

P4's outbox, stable idempotency keys and inline legible provenance remain load-bearing and now carry deterministic dispatcher enforcement rather than advisory hints, answering C3's enforcement-drift risk without turning every write into ceremony. The Engagement-scoped append-only log is a bounded scope addition, not a redesign.

report:
COUNCIL RECORD - run council-msg1rnli-54c70567. Status: INCOMPLETE. Chairman procedural only; the chairman did not research, propose, align, or vote.

PROCEDURAL RECORD. A five-seat roster was confirmed and checkpointed: C1 Atlas (systems coherence and long-term architecture), C2 Forge (pragmatic delivery, simplicity, operational cost), C3 Cassandra (adversarial risk, failure modes, security), C4 Hearth (human, developer, product impact), C5 Horizon (innovation, optionality, future leverage), all on openai/gpt-5.6-luna, researchers on anthropic/claude-sonnet-5. The member fanout was launched three times. Attempt 1 lost all five seats to an upstream overloaded_error. Attempt 2 returned C3 and C4, each having dispatched its two researchers and filed one proposal. Attempt 3 lost C1, C2 and C5 again. Those three seats therefore exhausted their two permitted replacements without producing research or a proposal, which is the sole reason this run is published as INCOMPLETE rather than CONSENSUS. Two seats survived, so strict majority is floor(2/2)+1 = 2, meaning acceptance required unanimity of the surviving seats.

The proposal set was frozen at two proposals - P3 (Cassandra) and P4 (Hearth) - and checkpointed; no chairman-authored proposal was needed or created. Alignment ran for both surviving seats: C3 sponsored P3, C4 sponsored P4, each declared a medium P3/P4 conflict and filed direct challenges, and both returned readyToVote=true. Because direct challenges and a medium conflict existed, one alignment-debate response round was run before voting; it produced genuine movement rather than restatement. The ballot then returned YES/YES from both seats on both proposals. Because both accepted proposals carried a declared conflict, exactly one reconciliation round with a complete re-vote was run; both seats independently stated the conflict resolved on the same merged terms and re-affirmed YES on both proposals. Every phase was checkpointed before the next began. Seat identities, biases, models and attempt numbers are preserved in the members, research, readiness, votes and reconciliationRounds sections.

TALLY. P3 - Fenced Engagements plus Taint-Gated Authority (C3 Cassandra, attempt 2, confidence 0.72): YES from C3, YES from C4. Accepted, 2 of 2. P4 - Engagement-scoped shared understanding (C4 Hearth, attempt 2, confidence 0.72): YES from C3, YES from C4. Accepted, 2 of 2. No NO votes were cast. C1, C2 and C5 cast no ballots because they never executed.

SUBSTANTIVE OUTCOME. Both surviving seats independently rejected the two obvious models and converged on the same hybrid. A single serialized shared conversation was rejected because it is a literal head-of-line-blocking bottleneck, because it collapses every private disclosure into one org-visible transcript, and because persistence turns one successful indirect prompt injection into a standing organisational instruction. Independent per-human sessions were rejected as split brain by construction - divergent belief, lost updates, duplicate Ghosts, contradictory commitments with no arbiter. The accepted answer is that Albus is one colleague because its durable organisational state is one artifact, not because its conversation is one thread.

The irreducible primitives, on which both proposals agree, are: ENGAGEMENT, a durable topic-scoped aggregate (a feature, order, exception or investigation) that outlives every AgentSession and deployment and is the unit of coherence; a versioned BELIEF RECORD or Belief Set carrying per-element provenance, confidence and trust label; COMMITMENT, a self-issued, assessable, state-machined promise that always names a human owner-of-outcome alongside Albus as executor, so accountability never evaporates into the agent; CLAIM, a soft expiring lock that deduplicates overlapping work at intake; and QUESTION or Clarification, a first-class addressable non-blocking record carrying an addressee, a stated default assumption and an expiry, so Albus parks one branch and proceeds elsewhere rather than blocking, with downstream Ghosts marked provisional and any applied default logged as agent-defaulted. Authority is carried by intent-bound expiring grants scoped to irreversible-effect classes, checked against graph-governed role rather than against whoever happened to ask, and DISCLOSURE SCOPE labels keep private context person-scoped: Albus may act on a private constraint but must not restate it, recording instead a non-attributive derived belief plus a marker that a constraint exists and who holds it - never silent leakage and never silent ignoring.

The reconciliation produced four binding merged terms. First, concurrency is pure optimistic compare-and-set on Engagement writes with no leases, because Ghost review as the write gate reduces a stale writer to a rejected Ghost; C3 withdrew its lease requirement on that argument. Second, at the effect boundary no AgentRun calls an integration directly: the winning commit writes a transactional outbox intent row and a single-writer dispatcher performs the call with an idempotency key derived from stable external identity, never from mutable run state, with a declared compensation per action class. This closed C3's concrete failure scenario in which two runs key a supplier chase on different Belief Set digests, produce two unique keys, defeat intake dedupe and send two conflicting chases with no Ghost in between - under the outbox design a fenced-out run has no call site. Third, taint lands at the first non-human ingestion path and is surfaced inline on Ghosts and intent rows with tainted spans and source document visible rather than as a laundered summary, and the dispatcher deterministically refuses to auto-dispatch an irreversible or externally visible action whose causal instruction is tainted and refuses batches mixing tainted with untainted items, while never gating reading, drafting, Ghost creation or internal belief writes. C3 withdrew universal gating on C4's evidence that a control which fires on everything trains rubber-stamping; C4 withdrew deferral on C3's argument that role governance answers who may act but not what persuaded the agent to ask. A calibration tripwire binds both: gate firing above roughly one in five effect-boundary actions, or promotion approval above roughly 95 percent, indicates miscalibration and must narrow or defer the gate. Fourth, the audit boundary is extended from session-scoped to an Engagement-scoped append-only event log, append-only by database grant, because a Commitment that outlives its session cannot be evidenced by that session's log; hash chaining was conceded as optional later hardening after C3 could name no in-scope adversary it defeats.

On current Ameba architecture, both seats agreed on what is EXTENDED - one Agent and one AgentCore Runtime, Trigger-creates-AgentSession, AgentRuns, Ghost and Integration Action review gating (extended with idempotency keys, sagas and compensations), and Memory (extended with scope partitioning, sanitisation, TTL and integrity checks) - and on what must be OVERTURNED: interactive chat as the container of shared understanding (chat stays per-human for throughput but is no longer where coherence lives); cross-session state flowing only through governed graph data, Session Handoffs, Context Files or Memory, since none of those can express versioned belief, ownership or contradiction; the per-session scratch workspace as the only working store; and the session-scoped event log as the audit boundary. Session Handoffs and Context Files become projections of Engagement state rather than the carriers of it. The three-way separation both seats insisted on: durable organisational state is the Engagement, its Commitments, Ghosts and the governed graph; conversational transcript is session-scoped citable evidence and never authority; learned Memory is generalised preference and skill and never a substitute for either.

The social protocol, which both seats treated as the actual answer rather than the storage design, is this: Albus publishes its mental model instead of holding it privately. Every turn opens with a one-line grounding statement naming what it believes, who asked for what, what it has promised and to whom, and what it is waiting for - the cheap evidence of understanding that completes a contribution. Its promises are self-issued and explicitly accepted, counter-offered or declined with a reason, never inferred obligation, and every promise is assessable and closed with a report. Contradictory instructions are never silently arbitrated or resolved by recency: the conflict is recorded, the affected Commitment freezes, both instructions are named to both requesters plus the accountable owner, unaffected work continues, and escalation to a designated decider expires rather than deadlocking. Proactive communication is addressed to the specific owner or asker, batched, and always a state delta rather than a nudge. The human-visible surface is one Engagement page - Believes, Doing, Promised, Waiting For, Completed - with each row traceable to provenance and principal, plus a per-person commitments-to-me view and batched risk-tiered review. Errors trigger an explicit repair protocol: acknowledge, explain cause, state the correction, re-promise. Both seats were explicit that this must not degrade into an inbox or task queue - a queue shows work but not belief, waiting or promise provenance, which is precisely what makes a colleague trustworthy - and both insisted legibility must ship before autonomy, since shipping autonomy first is the documented path to review surrender.

RECORDED DISSENT AND CONDITIONS. C3 Cassandra votes YES on P4 conditional on the no-auto-dispatch rule being a deterministic dispatcher-side precondition with a merge-blocking test rather than advisory guidance, and warns that legible provenance is weaker than a hard block absent calibration telemetry. C4 Hearth votes YES on P3 conditional on Authority Grants and taint gating remaining bound to irreversible-effect classes only, never to reading, drafting or Ghost creation, or the re-grant treadmill returns; and conditional on Integration Action keys being pinned to stable external identity. Both seats' unresolved risks stand on the record: Belief Record poisoning becoming durable organisational truth, Engagement mis-resolution silently splitting one topic in two, disclosure-promotion pressure eroding privacy boundaries, approval and notification fatigue collapsing review into rubber-stamping, conflict deadlock when the decider is absent, compensations that are not achievable in the real world once an email is sent or a supplier told, and audit gaps that make an action unattributable to a principal.

WEIGHT OF THIS RESULT. The substantive convergence is strong and was reached through genuine concession rather than restatement, but it rests on two seats out of five. The absent perspectives are material to this specific question: C2 Forge would have tested whether the Engagement aggregate, outbox, dispatcher and Engagement-scoped audit log are worth their build and operating cost against a cheaper design; C1 Atlas would have tested the aggregate boundary and long-term coherence of adding a new durable primitive; C5 Horizon would have tested whether the model scales to many concurrent workstreams without fragmenting Albus's identity. Neither surviving seat carried a cost-scepticism or optionality brief, and both share a bias toward adding governance machinery, so the merged design should be read as under-challenged on cost, aggregate-boundary choice and future scaling. The recommended follow-up is to re-run the missing three seats against the frozen P3/P4 merged terms before treating this as a settled architectural decision.
